messages:
alex: Heads up — after the Triton routing change yesterday I'm seeing a 12-18% p50 latency increase for seq_len=1024 on A100 pools. Not all traffic, mostly long-context chat requests.
jamie: Ugh. Which code path is falling back to CUTLASS? I thought Triton was the default for large mats.
marta: @jamie I added a small change to fallback heuristics so kernels that time out in autotune skip back to CUTLASS. It was supposed to reduce tail failures, but maybe we flipped the inequality for sequence length.
samir: Can you paste the routing check?
marta: Sure — here's the snippet I pushed: 
```
if (estimated_ms > autotune_threshold_ms && architecture == PCIe) {
  route = CUDA_CUTLASS;
} else {
  route = TRITON;
}
```
jamie: That `architecture == PCIe` check is brittle — on DGX-A100 that should be NVLink. If it matched unexpectedly it would force CUTLASS.
alex: Perf profile from prod (sampler) — p50/p95 for seq=512 vs 1024:
```
seq=512: Triton p50 18ms, p95 60ms
seq=1024: Triton p50 42ms, p95 120ms
CUTLASS fallback: seq=1024 p50 34ms, p95 130ms
```
alex: So Triton was still better at p50 for 1024 on some pods, but we routed many of them to CUTLASS and got higher p50 overall.
samir: Interesting that CUTLASS p95 is worse. Might be starvation/queue effects from different batching patterns.
jamie: What does the batching heuristic do differently between the runtimes? IIRC Triton does continuous batching and can pack different seq lengths more efficiently.
marta: Exactly. Triton path uses dynamic bucketized batching + auto-prefix cache awareness. CUTLASS path uses fixed micro-batches tuned for shorter sequences — so when long sequences are forced there, it degrades.
alex: I captured a perf trace from the slow pod. Key bits:
- KV cache hot hits ~82%
- tail requests with cache misses spike seq length and kernel sizes
- fallback decisions logged ~30% of 1024 requests

Trace snippet:
```
[1748001301] route_candidate: TRITON (est_ms=45)
[1748001301] autotune_probe: timeout -> fallback to CUTLASS
[1748001301] enqueue -> increased microbatch wait 12ms
[1748001303] kernel_execute CUDA_CUTLASS ms=38
```
jamie: That autotune timeout is suspiciously short. What is autotune_threshold_ms currently?
marta: 40ms. The probes run with a 30ms timeout for early exit, so racey. I think a couple of harmless slow probes turned into permanent routing decisions because we cache the last-good route too aggressively.
samir: We should make fallback decisions aggregated over a sliding window rather than per-probe. Also factor in sequence-length distribution: if >60% of recent traffic is long, prefer Triton even if a few probes time out.
alex: Proposed quick fix: 1) bump probe timeout to 80ms; 2) only mark route as degraded if 3/5 probes fail; 3) add seq_len_weight to route score. Anyone opposed?
jamie: +1 on the sliding-window gating. But bumping probe timeout might slow down cold routing. Maybe do exponential backoff: short probes usually, but if hotspot shows long seqs, run extended validation probes.
marta: I'll prepare a patch. Also want to log kernel selection score for each decision so we can post-hoc analyze. Example score formula: `score = base_perf - alpha * failed_probes + beta * seq_len_factor + gamma * kv_hit_rate`.
alex: Can we instrument KV cache behavior in the decision? For example, if kv_hit_rate > 0.7 favor higher-throughput Triton path since it amortizes KV costs.
samir: Good idea. Also include batch_size_variance — Triton handles variance better.
ci-bot: deploy-check: proposed change (marta/feat/router-wins) has 3 unit tests failing (routing_test: fallback_sliding_window).
jamie: I'll take the test failures. Likely mocks for time window need adjustment.
alex: For rollouts: put change behind a dynamic flag and enable on a subset of pods (10%) with monitoring alerts on p50 regression >5%.
marta: Agreed. I'll add telemetry counters: route_chosen, probe_latency, probe_fail_count, seq_len_distribution_bucket, kv_hit_rate.
alex: After patch, let's run the offline perf sweep across seq lengths [128,256,512,1024,2048] on both NVLink and PCIe nodes. Capture p50/p95 and batching metrics.
samir: Also include a synthetic workload with KV misses to stress fallback.
jamie: One more note: CUTLASS autotune table is per-arch + sm capability. If we see too many fallbacks on A100, we might need to refresh the autotune table; some kernels got new heuristics in last release.
marta: I'll add a migration job: refresh-autotune --target a100 --force-probe.
alex: Cool. Timeline: patch + tests today, flag rollout tomorrow morning, sweep + autotune job mid-day. Keep thread updated with results. :thumbsup:
samir: I'll watch the dashboards and post anomalies.
marta: Patch PR: https://git.internal/redwood/infra/+/2345 (will update tests)
jamie: Thanks all. Hopefully quick win.
alex: Thanks everyone — saved a heap of context for postmortem if needed.
